options.explanation: Speed is a kinetic matter, not the gap here.

options.explanation: Enthalpy is precisely what fails here.
The spread of matter and energy carries these changes.
Activation energy governs rate, not direction.
Catalysts change rate, not feasibility.

options.text: Energetically more stable, because its energy is more spread out

questions.stem: A melting ice cube illustrates the entropy driver because

options.text: The ordered lattice becomes mobile liquid, spreading energy and particles more widely
options.explanation: Melting raises disorder without any energy gain to justify it enthalpically.
Melting absorbs energy, going the warmer way.

options.text: Ice has higher entropy than water
options.explanation: The liquid has the higher entropy.
Melting is endothermic.

questions.stem: State the two driving forces that determine whether a reaction occurs.
State the entropy-related reason a more disordered system is favoured.
questions.modelAnswer: A more disordered system is energetically more stable because its energy is spread out over more arrangements.

questions.stem: Explain why an endothermic reaction can still occur spontaneously.
questions.modelAnswer: The enthalpy penalty is paid for by a large entropy gain: if the products' matter and energy are spread over far more arrangements, the total change is favourable even though the system climbs the energy ladder.

questions.stem: A solid and a liquid react to give a gas, and the flask grows cold. Identify the enthalpy sign and the driving force.
questions.modelAnswer: The cooling flask marks an endothermic change, delta H positive; the reaction is driven by the large entropy rise as a gas forms from condensed phases.

options.text: The number of possible arrangements of particles and energy in a system
options.explanation: The definition is a count of ways.

options.text: The heat content of a system
options.explanation: Heat content is enthalpy's territory.

options.explanation: Each molecule alone has two options.

options.explanation: More particles mean more choices.
S grows with W.
All systems have entropy.

options.text: The number of arrangements grows explosively as particles multiply
options.explanation: Exponential growth in particle number is the point.

questions.stem: The equation linking entropy to the number of arrangements is

options.text: S = k ln W, with k the Boltzmann constant
options.explanation: The logarithm tames the explosive count.
A linear form would explode even faster than W.
The logarithm is essential.
The constant multiplies, not divides.

questions.stem: Once the cover slip separating two gas jars is removed, the molecules spread evenly because

options.explanation: Nature samples the many-ways state most often.

options.text: The molecules are attracted to glass

Weight is unchanged.

questions.stem: State the value of W for five molecules spread between two gas jars.
State the equation linking entropy to arrangements and the constant's units.
questions.modelAnswer: S = k ln W, with k = 1.38 x 10^-23 J K^-1 mol^-1.

questions.stem: Explain why the number of arrangements grows exponentially with particle count.
questions.modelAnswer: Every particle's two choices multiply the whole system's possibilities, so adding a particle doubles the count; N particles therefore give 2^N arrangements, the signature of exponential growth.

questions.stem: Ten molecules can spread between two jars. State W and compare it with the five-molecule case.
questions.modelAnswer: W = 2^10 = 1024, thirty-two times the five-molecule count of 32, showing the explosive growth of options with particle number.

options.text: More energy quanta become available to distribute among the particles

options.explanation: Entropy rises with temperature.

options.text: Higher temperature, more quanta, more arrangements, higher entropy

options.text: Higher temperature, fewer quanta, lower entropy

questions.stem: State what quanta are and the whole-number rule.
questions.modelAnswer: Quanta are packets of energy, and only whole numbers of them can be held or transferred.

questions.stem: State the effect of raising temperature on the number of energy arrangements.
questions.modelAnswer: It increases the number of quanta to share, raising the number of arrangements and hence the entropy.

questions.stem: Explain why only whole numbers of quanta make energy distribution countable.
questions.modelAnswer: If energy came in continuous amounts, infinitely many distributions would exist and counting arrangements would be meaningless; the whole-number rule keeps the count finite, which is what makes entropy a combinatorial quantity.

questions.stem: A crystal is warmed from 300 K to 600 K. Describe the change in its energy arrangements.
questions.modelAnswer: The crystal's particles hold more quanta at 600 K, so the number of ways of distributing that energy among them rises steeply, and the crystal's entropy increases accordingly.
